title: Deterministic polynomial construction of strong thin spanning trees
exact_target: Is there an absolute C and a deterministic algorithm polynomial in total binary input length that, on every k-edge-connected finite loopless multigraph (parallel-edge multiplicities allowed), returns a spanning tree T with |T intersect $\delta (S)|<=C|\delta (S)|/k$ for every vertex cut S?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
\paragraph{Statement recorded in the supplied source.}
Is there an absolute C and a deterministic algorithm polynomial in total binary input length that, on every k-edge-connected finite loopless multigraph (parallel-edge multiplicities allowed), returns a spanning tree T with |T intersect $\delta (S)|<=C|\delta (S)|/k$ for every vertex cut S?

\subsection{Short English statement}
Is there an absolute C and a deterministic algorithm polynomial in total binary input length that, on every k-edge-connected finite loopless multigraph (parallel-edge multiplicities allowed), returns a spanning tree T with |T intersect $\delta (S)|<=C|\delta (S)|/k$ for every vertex cut S?
